page: Vultr voc-g-8c-32gb-160s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance built on the x86_64 architecture. The server is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC processor running at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz, offering 8 vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with two threads per core. Hardware specifications include 32.0 GB of system memory, delivering a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU, paired with a bundled 160 GB local NVMe SSD and one complimentary public IPv4 address. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, with hardware instruction support for AES, SHA-NI, BMI2, and FMA, while lacking AVX-512 extensions.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core compute capabilities, with stress-ng single-core execution scoring in the top 25 percent of tested systems. Multi-threaded processing falls within the middle 50 percent, demonstrated by a multi-core stress-ng metric of 23301.5 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8912.0. Memory throughput remains steady under uncached transfers, registering 117.03 GB/sec on large read blocks and 77.42 GB/sec on writes. In application-specific testing, the server achieved 15.29 million Redis SET operations per second and 8.45 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. A measurable performance limitation appears in heavier compute loads like medium-model 7B LLM prompt processing, where lack of vector accelerator instructions places it in the bottom 25 percent.

From an infrastructure cost perspective, the instance provides favorable resource density by pairing dedicated AMD EPYC compute allocations with high-speed local NVMe storage on a single virtualized slice. Because CPU capacity is dedicated rather than shared, workloads are shielded from noisy-neighbor throttling. The configuration is appropriate for sustained multi-threaded tasks, including production web serving, backend relational databases, Redis caching layers, software compilation, and CI/CD worker nodes.
description: Vultr voc-g-8c-32gb-160s-amd is a general-purpose virtual machine within the Optimized Cloud Compute family, configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs spanning 4 physical AMD EPYC cores at a 2.0 GHz clock rate. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 32.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio alongside a 160 GB local NVMe SSD. The processor features 16 MB of L3 cache and supports hardware encryption extensions including AES and SHA-NI, though it lacks AVX-512 support. Benchmark data reflects top-quartile single-core performance in stress-ng evaluations, complemented by solid mid-tier throughput across multi-core tests, memory bandwidth, and Redis transactions exceeding 15 million operations per second. However, medium-tier language model prompt processing reveals bottom-quartile throughput. The balance of dedicated compute cores, local NVMe storage, and standard memory density makes this instance well matched for web serving, database operations, software compilation, and CI/CD pipelines.
